summary: AI code generation has become mainstream in 2026, with JetBrains research reporting weekly AI coding-agent use among 90% of professional developers and daily use among 68%. GitHub Copilot remains the enterprise default by raw user count, while Cursor has become the everyday shipping IDE and Claude Code the preferred tool for genuinely hard, autonomous coding tasks. The market has consolidated around a handful of agentic, multi-model tools that integrate deeply with IDEs, terminals, and CI/CD pipelines.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
strengths: Largest install base with 20M+ users
Widest IDE and provider range with multi-model selector
Agent Mode for autonomous multi-step changes
SOC 2 compliance and fits inside existing Microsoft enterprise agreements
Cloud agents can be assigned issues and open PRs
tools.best_for: The pragmatic enterprise default integrated across the Microsoft and GitHub ecosystem

tools.name: Cursor
strengths: Best-in-class multi-file intelligence
In-editor model switching across multiple frontier providers
Inline diff-based apply with developer approval
Cloud agents and Cursor CLI
The tool developers actively request from procurement
tools.best_for: The default AI IDE for everyday shipping and multi-file edits

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Claude Pro $20/mo and Max $100-200/mo; API usage-based
strengths: Strongest coding brain with highest SWE-bench scores
Terminal-native autonomous agent that plans, edits files, and runs shell commands
Largest context window
High agentic autonomy for genuinely hard problems
tools.best_for: Complex, hard problems requiring deep autonomous reasoning

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.pricing_paid: Included with ChatGPT Plus $20/mo, Pro $200/mo; API usage-based
strengths: Cloud-based agentic coding agent that works in parallel on tasks
Deep integration with ChatGPT and GPT frontier models
CLI and IDE extensions for autonomous task execution
Strong code generation and refactoring
tools.best_for: Delegating parallel autonomous coding tasks within the OpenAI ecosystem

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
strengths: Deep AWS integration for cloud-native development
Agentic code transformation and Java/.NET upgrades
Security scanning and remediation
Enterprise IAM and compliance support
tools.best_for: AWS-centric development, migrations, and cloud workflows

tools.name: Devin Desktop
strengths: Autonomous software engineer that completes end-to-end tasks
Inherits Codeium/Windsurf's strong IDE heritage
Parallel agent execution on complex tickets
Integrates with Slack, GitHub, and CI/CD
tools.best_for: Fully autonomous end-to-end feature and ticket completion

tools.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
strengths: Native integration across all JetBrains IDEs
Context-aware completion tuned to project structure
Junie agentic coding agent for autonomous tasks
Multi-model support
tools.best_for: Developers working within the JetBrains IDE ecosystem

tools.name: Windsurf
strengths: Agentic Cascade flow for multi-step autonomous edits
Clean AI-native editor experience
Strong codebase awareness and context retrieval
Continued development under Cognition
tools.best_for: AI-native agentic coding in a dedicated editor

tools.name: Tabnine
strengths: Privacy-first with self-hosted and air-gapped deployment
Enterprise code governance and compliance
Personalized models trained on private codebases
Multi-model support under Tricentis ownership

tools.name: RooCode
strengths: Reliability-first agent for large, complex changes
Open-source and highly configurable
Multi-model support via bring-your-own-key
Strong autonomous multi-file refactoring
tools.best_for: Reliable autonomous execution of big codebase changes
